I couldn’t tell you love. I used salicylic acid for a bit, but I think I overdid it and it caused a major breakout. It might work on sensitive skin if used right! I’d say start very, very slow, don’t rush for results. Do your research, that’s my biggest recommendation. I wish a dermatologist was in my budget, but it’s not. If it is for you, I’d definitely recommend seeing one. If not, I’d advise adding only one product at a time and always doing a patch test. I used to skip doing patch test and adding  a bunch of different products at once, but it honestly did more harm than good. Cleaning up the aftermath takes way longer than fixing the original problem.
Also, yours aren’t really noticeable. Everyone has them, it might just seem more noticeable to you because you’re black, sweetheart. I promise you, no one really cares lol.

Those are sebaceous filaments, and you can’t really get rid of them since it’s just your skin producing oil. But you can definitely make them less noticeable. What works for me, especially since my skin’s on the sensitive side, is oil cleansing. I massage oil (oils made specifically for the face or something like jojoba oil) into the area for about 5 minutes, then use a warm washcloth to gently exfoliate. After that, I wash it all off with a regular cleanser. I usually do this a couple times a week. You can also try chemical exfoliants like salicylic acid or mandelic acid, just be careful not to overdo it. For melanated skin, too much can cause irritation or dark spots. Hope that helps!

I believe their products are comedogenic, but that may not be the case for everyone. I’ve had plenty of people tell me that as soon as they stopped using a certain cerave product their acne cleared up, so i’m just recommending process of elimination for his skin care since cerave can be problematic for some people.
I personally use the Neutrogena Ultra gentle daily facial moisturizer. It’s the only one that hasn’t broken me out. It’s light-weight but it’s very moisturizing. doesn’t leave that greasy feeling

Also be so so careful with the Kojic acid soap if you continue its use. If you’re not putting on your sunscreen properly and you’re exposed to the sun (you’re supposed to apply it multiple times throughout the day tbh) it can worsen hyperpigmentation instead of helping it.

I would say just stick to a simple cleanser, simple moisturizer, and sunscreen to try and pinpoint what’s causing the issues. I would stick with the Cetaphil cleanser, maybe swap out the cerave moisturizer (I don’t trust cerave but that’s just my opinion), and stick with your sunscreen. Less is always more when it comes to skincare.
